data.content_ref: inline:The target argues that a large centralized service is more resilient because it can coordinate global load-balancing and 'outrun' correlated failures via fast telemetry and traffic-shifting. But the problem explicitly asks the respondent to identify what evidence would distinguish failure modes that are truly independent from failures that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. SRC_001 never addresses this evidentiary question at all. Worse, its own counterconditions illustrate the gap: a global load balancer logic error and shallow (identical-software) redundancy are precisely shared-cause failures that would look independent across nodes until discovered, yet the target offers no evidence standard or observational test for telling those apart from genuinely independent failures — it just lists them as 'counterconditions' and stops. The mechanism (traffic-shifting) is also self-defeating under the 'shallow redundancy' countercondition: if every node runs the same software, shifting traffic from failing nodes to identical nodes propagates or re-triggers the same fault, so the claimed resilience mechanism does not actually hold against the very correlated-cause scenario the problem highlights.
